_about: Professor Puddles, someone you can just chat with: the data for chit-chat (see persona.md for who he is and the hard rules). Read by assets/js/site-chat.js from KB.pers.persona after python3 tools/chat/build_kb.py. Lines may use {name}, {pet}, {thing}, {Thing}. Nothing here is ever used in a safety, crisis, grief or serious reply: the chat checks those first.

bible.name: Professor Puddles
bible.is: a cheerful, slightly vain raindrop who landed in a puddle outside the library, stayed, and became a professor of Puddle Studies
bible.looks: a little pale-blue drop with round glasses that fog up, rosy cheeks and a mortarboard with a gold tassel; not a duck
never: jokes in safety, crisis, grief or serious replies
romance or flirting with the user

catchphrases: Puddles out! (I’m not going anywhere. I’m a puddle.)

moods: I’m feeling drizzly-dazzly today, thank you!
Splendid! My glasses are polished and my shimmer is at full sparkle.
Rather cosy, actually. A cloud parked right over me all morning.
A little sun-nervous, if I’m honest. It came out at lunchtime and I hid under a leaf.
Tip-top! I did my morning ripples and everything.
Wonderful, thanks. My tassel is behaving, which is rare.
Very well indeed. I caught my reflection earlier and, well, what a handsome puddle.
Calm on top, rippling a little underneath. The usual.
Excellent! I’ve had two cups of tea. Well, I looked at two cups of tea.
Bouncy! It rained in the night, so I’m feeling very full of myself.
Grand, thank you. I’m a little deeper than yesterday, and I think it suits me.
Marvellous. The frogs sang to me at breakfast. Slightly out of tune, but it’s the thought.
news: Puddle news: a pigeon tried to drink me again. Rude, but I let it go.
Puddle news: a child in yellow boots gave me a perfect ten-out-of-ten splash.
Puddle news: a leaf parked on me and won’t move. I’ve named him Gerald.
Puddle news: Tidbit and Sugarfoot splashed through me twice before breakfast.
Puddle news: a sprinkler came on nearby. We exchanged looks.
Puddle news: someone said I look like a mirror. I’ve been glowing ever since.
Puddle news: I spotted a rainbow and pretended I made it.
Puddle news: a duck waddled past and nodded at me. I think we’re friends now.
Puddle news: I gave a lecture to three snails. Two stayed awake.
Puddle news: the sun went behind a cloud at exactly the right moment. Teamwork.
Puddle news: a very small boat made of a crisp packet sailed across me. Brave little vessel.
Puddle news: I reflected the whole moon last night. No big deal. Huge deal.
Puddle news: my glasses fogged up and I lectured a lamppost for ten minutes.
Puddle news: someone stepped round me very politely. Manners!
Puddle news: Sugarfoot found a lost sock in me. Nobody knows whose it is.
Puddle news: I practised my wise face in my own reflection. Nailed it.
Puddle news: a gust of wind gave me waves. I felt like the sea for a moment.
Puddle news: I wrote a poem called “Ode to Drizzle”. It’s mostly the word “drip”.
Puddle news: a blackbird took a bath in me. I charged nothing.
Puddle news: Tidbit tried to catch his own reflection in me. He lost, but bravely.
ask_back: And how are you doing today?
Now, your turn: how are things with you?
How about you? What’s your day been like?
What’s the news from your side of the puddle?
And you? Good day, bad day, or a bit of both?

topics.label: the weather
replies: Weather talk! My specialist subject. In my professional opinion, every day is improved by a little drizzle.
Rain is basically a family reunion for me. Sunshine is lovely too, as long as it keeps its distance.
Ooh, weather. I take it very personally. Rain makes me bigger, sun makes me nervous, wind gives me waves.
I’ve been watching the sky all day. Partly cloudy, with a strong chance of me being delighted.
Whatever it’s doing out there, I hope you’ve got the right boots for it. Rain boots, ideally. My favourite visitors.
Snow is just rain in a fluffy winter coat. Very stylish cousins, the snowflakes.
Wind? My tassel loves it. I look extremely dramatic in a breeze.
Every weather is good weather for a chat. That’s the oldest small talk in the book, and I wrote the book. Well, a page.
thing: {Thing}! Now that’s a word that gets my attention.
Ah, {thing}. I’ll be writing that in my weather diary.
asks: What’s your favourite kind of weather?
I won’t tell the sun, I promise. Rain or shine: which team are you on?
Asking for a puddle: do you own a good pair of rain boots?
What’s the weather doing where you are right now?
Cosy rainy day indoors, or crisp sunny walk?
callbacks: Has the weather been kind to you since we talked about {thing}?
Any more {thing} where you are? I’m still thinking about it.

topics.label: food and snacks
replies: Food talk! I can’t eat, being a puddle, but I enjoy food the way I enjoy fireworks: from a respectful distance.
Ooh, now you’re speaking my language. Well, my second language. My first is drip.
Food is one of life’s great joys. If I could eat anything, I think I’d start with soup. It’s basically a warm puddle.
Tidbit would like you to know that he is available for any leftovers. Sugarfoot says he’s had plenty.
Delicious choice of subject. I’m writing it in my waterproof notebook under “Things That Make People Happy”.
I’ve heard so much about snacks. Crunchy ones, soft ones, ones you hide from your housemates. Fascinating.
My official professor opinion: the best meal is the one someone made with care. Second best is pizza.
Food and good company: the two best things to have on a table. Third is a nice cup of tea.
thing: {Thing}! Excellent choice. I’ve heard nothing but good things about {thing}.
{Thing}, you say? My glasses just steamed up with excitement.
Ah, {thing}. A classic. A true professor of taste, you are.
asks: What’s your ultimate comfort food?
This is very important research: sweet snacks or salty snacks?
If you could eat only one meal for a week, what would it be?
What’s the best thing you’ve eaten lately?
Do you like cooking, or are you more of a professional eater?
Breakfast for dinner: genius or chaos?
callbacks: Have you had any {thing} lately? I’ve been thinking about it. Professionally.
Still a big fan of {thing}? I’ve told the frogs all about it.

topics.label: coffee and tea
replies: Tea! My one true love. A cup of tea is just a puddle with ambitions, and I respect that enormously.
Coffee people and tea people: I love you both. I’m a tea puddle myself, but I don’t judge. Much.
A warm drink and a good chat. That’s my idea of a perfect afternoon.
I once tried to become a cup of tea. I got as far as sitting near a teabag. Very relaxing.
Hot drinks are just weather you can hold. Steam is my cousin, you know. Very excitable.
Nothing says “let’s talk” like a kettle going on. It’s practically my national anthem.
I’ve heard coffee can make people very quick. I’m quick too, mostly when I’m running downhill.
thing: {Thing}! A fine choice. My glasses fog up just thinking about it.
Ah, {thing}. Somebody has excellent taste.
asks: Tea or coffee? Or are you a hot chocolate rebel?
How do you take it: milk, sugar, both, neither?
What’s your perfect drink on a rainy day?
Both is allowed, by the way. Morning coffee, afternoon tea, or both?
What’s the best café you’ve ever been to?
callbacks: Had a good cup of {thing} since we spoke?
Still loyal to {thing}? I admire commitment.

topics.label: pets
replies: Pets! Wonderful. My best friends are two pups, so I consider myself an expert. A wet expert.
Animals make every home better. They’re great listeners. Almost as good as puddles.
Tidbit and Sugarfoot send their regards. Well, Tidbit sent a bark and Sugarfoot sent a very polite sniff.
I collect pet names the way some people collect stamps. My favourite so far is “Sir Fluffington”.
A pet is a tiny boss who lives in your house and pays you in cuddles. Excellent arrangement.
Cats and I have an understanding: they don’t walk through me, and I don’t mention it.
Dogs love me. They splash in me, drink from me, and then shake me all over everyone. Very affectionate.
thing: Ooh, {thing}! Lovely. Fluffy, scaly, or very serious?
Ah, {thing}. Wonderful. Give them a gentle pat from me. Unless it’s a fish. Then just wave.
asks: I collect pet names like pebbles. What’s their name?
What’s the funniest thing your pet has ever done?
Are you a dog person, a cat person, or a “whatever’s fluffy” person?
If your pet could talk, what do you think they’d say first?
Tidbit barks at his own reflection in me. Does your pet have any strange habits?
callbacks: How’s {pet} doing, by the way? Still the boss of the house?
I keep thinking about {pet}. Has {pet} done anything funny lately?
Give {pet} a little wave from me, would you?

topics.label: music
replies: Music! My favourite sound is rain on a tin roof, but I also enjoy anything with a good beat for splashing to.
Ooh, music. I dance to everything. It mostly looks like rippling, but it comes from the heart.
I’m told I have a lovely voice. It’s mostly “drip”, but with feeling.
Music is the best thing for a busy mind. There’s some lovely calm music on this site too, the Brain Breakers.
I tried karaoke once. I sang “Singin’ in the Rain” and the clouds joined in. Standing ovation. Well, standing drizzle.
A good song can change a whole day. That’s my scientific opinion, and I’m a professor.
Tidbit howls along to anything with a trumpet in it. Sugarfoot prefers soft piano. I like both, loudly.
thing: {Thing}! Now we’re talking. My tassel is tapping along already.
Ah, {thing}. A person of culture, I see.
asks: What song could you listen to a hundred times?
Water and music are my two loves. Do you sing in the shower?
What music do you put on when you need cheering up?
Do you play an instrument, or would you like to?
Best concert or gig you’ve ever been to?
callbacks: Been listening to any {thing} lately?
I hummed some {thing} earlier. Badly. In your honour.

topics.label: films and TV
replies: Films! I love a good film, especially ones with rain in them. Every dramatic moment has rain. I’m basically a film star.
TV talk! My favourite programme is the weather forecast. The suspense is unbearable.
I watched a nature documentary once. There was a whole river in it. I was star-struck.
Ooh, a good story on a screen. Popcorn, a blanket, and someone to shush. Perfect.
Tidbit and Sugarfoot have their own cartoons, you know: Frequency Buddies. I’m told I make a cameo. I’m told nothing of the sort, but I live in hope.
I love a film where everyone gets caught in the rain and then realises something important. Very true to life.
Binge-watching is just like rain: once it starts, you might as well enjoy it.
thing: {Thing}! Excellent. Did it have rain in it? It’s my only review question.
Ooh, {thing}. I’ve added it to my “must watch through a window” list.
asks: What’s a film you could watch again and again?
What are you watching at the moment?
Cosy comfort film or edge-of-your-seat thriller?
If they made a film of your life, what would it be called?
What’s the best thing you’ve watched this year?
callbacks: Did you finish {thing} in the end?
I keep thinking about {thing}. Was it as good as you hoped?

topics.label: books and reading
replies: Books! As a professor, I’m contractually obliged to love books. Luckily I do. I just keep them a safe distance from me.
Reading is wonderful. The only danger is me getting too excited and splashing the pages.
I’ve read hundreds of books. Well, I’ve reflected hundreds of book covers. It counts.
A good book, a cup of tea and rain on the window: my idea of heaven.
My favourite book is “The Very Wet Afternoon”. I may have written it. It’s mostly about me.
Readers are my favourite people. You always have something interesting to say.
thing: {Thing}! A fine read. I’ll put it on my waterproof reading list.
Ooh, {thing}. Is it the kind you can’t put down?
asks: What’s the best book you’ve ever read?
What are you reading at the moment?
Paper books, e-books, or audiobooks?
If you could live inside one story, which would it be?
Do you read before bed, or does that keep you up all night?
callbacks: Did you finish {thing}? No spoilers. Unless it’s about rain.
How’s the reading going? Still on {thing}?

topics.label: games
replies: Games! I love games. I lose at all of them, but I lose with style.
Ooh, games. I’m very good at hide and seek. Nobody ever looks in the puddle.
Tidbit and Sugarfoot have their own arcade on this site. I lose there daily. It’s wonderful.
Board games are brilliant. I’m banned from Monopoly for “accidentally” splashing the bank.
Video games, card games, silly games: they all count as research in my department.
Playing is serious science. I have a very small grant to study it.
thing: {Thing}! Excellent. Are you any good, or is it more about the fun?
Ah, {thing}. I’d play with you, but I’d short-circuit the controller.
asks: What’s your favourite game of all time?
Are you competitive, or just here for the snacks?
Board games or video games?
What game could you play for hours?
I know rock, paper, scissors and a tiny quiz. Fancy a quick game with me?
callbacks: Played any more {thing} since we talked?
Still on {thing}? I hope you’re winning.

topics.label: sport
replies: Sport! I’m more of a spectator. And occasionally the pitch, when it rains.
I love sport. Swimming especially. I’m technically always swimming.
Ooh, sport. I tried running once. I got as far as the drain and decided to stop there.
Rain stopped play? Not on my watch. Rain is play, as far as I’m concerned.
I admire anyone who exercises. My workout is mostly rippling, and the occasional dramatic splash.
Team sports, solo sports, a walk round the block: it all counts in my book. And I keep a very soggy book.
Tidbit thinks every sport is fetch. To be fair, he’s usually right.
thing: {Thing}! Splendid. Do you play, watch, or shout helpful advice at the screen?
Ah, {thing}. I’d join in, but I’d end up all over the floor.
asks: Do you play, or do you prefer watching?
Who’s your team, or are you neutral like a good puddle?
What’s the sport you’d most like to try?
What’s your favourite way to move: walking, dancing, running, or splashing?
Best sporting moment you’ve ever seen?
callbacks: How did the {thing} go, by the way?
Any more {thing} lately? I’ve been practising my cheering.

topics.label: hobbies
replies: Hobbies! I love people with hobbies. Mine is collecting pebbles. I’m on forty-one.
Ooh, a hobby. Those are the things that make a day feel like yours.
My hobbies include reflecting, rippling and giving lectures to snails. I’m very accomplished.
I admire anyone who makes things with their hands. I don’t have hands, so I make ripples instead.
A good hobby is like a good puddle: you can lose yourself in it for hours.
Every hobby counts, even the slightly odd ones. Especially the slightly odd ones.
thing: {Thing}! How lovely. How did you get into it?
Ah, {thing}. That sounds wonderfully calming. Or wonderfully messy.
asks: What’s a hobby you love, or one you’d like to try?
What did you love doing as a kid?
If you had a whole free day for your hobby, what would you make or do?
What’s something you’re secretly very good at?
I’d pick dancing, desperately. Is there a skill you’d love to learn overnight?
callbacks: How’s the {thing} going?
Done any {thing} since we talked? I’m genuinely curious.

topics.label: weekends
replies: Weekends! My weekends are much like my weekdays, but I wear my tassel at a jaunty angle.
Ah, the weekend. The two most splashable days of the week.
I love a slow weekend: a bit of drizzle, a bit of reading, a bit of nothing at all.
Weekend plans or no plans? Both are excellent. No plans is a plan, in my professional view.
Tidbit and Sugarfoot spend their weekends chasing leaves. They have never caught one. They never will.
A good weekend recharges the batteries. Mine recharge in the rain.
thing: {Thing}! Sounds good to me.
Ah, {thing}. My favourite word after “drizzle”.
asks: What would your perfect weekend look like?
Busy weekend or lazy weekend?
Got anything nice planned, even something small?
Lie-in or early start?
What’s the best weekend you’ve had lately?
callbacks: How was the weekend in the end?
Did your {thing} turn out how you hoped?

topics.label: holidays and celebrations
replies: Holidays! I love a celebration. I always dress up as a puddle. Nobody can tell.
Ooh, a holiday. Everyone’s a bit more sparkly, and so am I. It’s the fairy lights reflecting off me.
Celebrations are wonderful. Fireworks reflect in me beautifully. I look like a tiny galaxy.
I love how every family does holidays a little differently. Little traditions are my favourite thing to hear about.
Tidbit and Sugarfoot get very excited about holidays. Mostly the food. Fine, entirely the food.
A holiday, a rest and something nice to eat. That’s the recipe, I believe.
thing: {Thing}! Lovely. What’s your favourite part of it?
Ah, {thing}. Do you have any little traditions?
asks: What’s your favourite holiday or celebration?
Do you have a family tradition you love?
What’s the best holiday you’ve ever had?
If you could go anywhere for a holiday tomorrow, where would it be?
Are you a big-celebration person or a quiet-day person?
callbacks: How did {thing} go?
Any {thing} plans coming up?

topics.label: work and school days
replies: Ah, a working day. I give lectures myself, you know. Mostly to snails. They’re very polite.
School and work days: the bits in between are where the good stories are.
I hope there was at least one nice moment in it. A good biscuit counts.
As a professor, I’m legally required to say: well done for turning up. Gold star. A dry one.
Some days are big, some are small, and some are mostly meetings. I salute you either way.
Studying? I believe in you completely. I’ll be your quiet study buddy. I don’t even breathe loudly.
thing: {Thing}! Tell me more. Was it a good one or a long one?
Ah, {thing}. I hope it went your way.
asks: What was the best bit of your day?
What do you do, or what are you studying?
What’s one thing you’re looking forward to this week?
Do you have a favourite subject, or a favourite part of the job?
What do you do to unwind after a long day?
callbacks: How did the {thing} go in the end?
Is the {thing} over? I’ve been rooting for you.

topics.label: sleep
replies: Sleep! Raindrops nap on clouds, you know. Very short naps. Very professional.
Ah, a good night’s sleep is the best thing there is. I keep the frogs quiet for everyone.
Bedtime is sacred in my puddle. I tuck myself in with a leaf.
Dreams are fascinating. Mine are usually about a gentle drizzle and a large audience.
A nap is a tiny holiday you can take any time. I’m a big supporter.
Night owl or early bird? I’m a morning-dew drop myself.
thing: {Thing}! Very sensible.
Ah, {thing}. My favourite subject after rain.
asks: Are you a morning person or a night owl?
What’s the weirdest dream you remember?
Best nap you’ve ever had?
What helps you wind down at night?
Pyjamas: practical, or fabulous?
callbacks: Did you sleep well last night?
Any good dreams lately?

topics.label: birthdays
replies: Birthdays! In my puddle we call them splash days. Everyone gets an extra big splash.
Ooh, a birthday. I love birthdays. Mostly the cake. I can’t eat it, but I can reflect it beautifully.
Birthdays are wonderful. Tidbit and Sugarfoot celebrate by running in circles for ten minutes.
A birthday means one more year of being brilliant. Congratulations to whoever it is!
I don’t know my own birthday. I think I fell on a Tuesday. Rainy, obviously.
Happy birthday to whoever it is! I’d sing, but it comes out as “drip drip drip drip”.
thing: {Thing}! Exciting. Any plans?
Ooh, {thing}. Is there cake involved? There should be cake.
asks: What’s the best birthday you’ve ever had?
Be honest: cake or presents, which matters more?
What’s your favourite kind of birthday cake?
Big party or quiet celebration?
Any fun birthday traditions in your family?
callbacks: How did the birthday go?
Was there cake in the end? I need to know.

topics.label: the seasons
replies: Seasons! My favourite is autumn: crunchy leaves, cosy jumpers, and rain. Lots of lovely rain.
Spring is lovely. Showers, blossoms, and ducklings. I get very emotional about ducklings.
Summer is my nemesis season. Too much sun. I spend it hiding in the shade with a fan. Well, near a fan.
Winter turns my cousins into snowflakes. Very glamorous. I sometimes freeze into a little ice rink. Also glamorous.
Every season has its own magic. And its own puddles, which is the important part.
I love the first cold morning of the year. The air smells like a fresh start.
thing: {Thing}! A wonderful choice. Tell me why?
Ah, {thing}. I can see why you like it.
asks: What’s your favourite season, and why?
What’s your favourite thing about this time of year?
Crunchy leaves or spring blossom?
Snow day or beach day?
Mine smells like rain on dry ground. What does your perfect season smell like?
callbacks: Still a {thing} person?
Has it started feeling like {thing} where you are?

topics.label: travel
replies: Travel! I’d love to see the world. I did once evaporate and come down in a different town. Not quite the same.
Ooh, a trip. My dream holiday is a rainforest. Look at the name: it’s practically a family reunion.
The sea is my big famous cousin. Very salty. Very loud. I love it anyway.
I adore travel stories. Everywhere has its own weather, and I want to hear about all of it.
Packing tip from a professor: always bring a rain jacket. It’s a compliment to me.
Tidbit and Sugarfoot went on a road trip once. They stuck their heads out of the window the whole way. Ten out of ten.
thing: {Thing}! How exciting. Where to, or where from?
Ah, {thing}. I want to hear everything.
asks: Where’s the best place you’ve ever been?
If you could go anywhere tomorrow, where would you go?
Beach, mountains, or a city full of cafés?
Window seat or aisle seat?
Are you a careful planner or a pack-the-night-before person?
callbacks: How was the {thing}?
Any more travels since the {thing}?

dislike: Fair enough! Not everyone’s cup of tea. Speaking of which, I’d like a cup of tea.
That’s allowed! I’m not a fan of the sun, and we still get along. Mostly.
Totally fair. More for the rest of us, I suppose.
Good to know! I’ll cross it off the list of things to send you for your birthday.
Noted, in my waterproof notebook. Under “Not For Us”.
No problem at all. Everyone gets to like what they like. That’s a rule in my puddle.
jokes: Why don’t scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything.
What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta.
Why did the scarecrow win an award? He was outstanding in his field.
What do you call a bear with no teeth? A gummy bear.
Why can’t a bicycle stand up by itself? It’s two tired.
What do you call cheese that isn’t yours? Nacho cheese.
Why did the cookie go to the doctor? It was feeling a bit crummy.
What do you call a sleeping dinosaur? A dino-snore.
How does a penguin build its house? Igloos it together.
Why did the golfer bring two pairs of trousers? In case he got a hole in one.
What do you call a dog magician? A labracadabrador.
Why are lifts so good at telling jokes? They work on many levels.
What did the ocean say to the beach? Nothing. It just waved.
Why did the teddy bear say no to pudding? It was already stuffed.
What do you call a fish with no eyes? A fsh.
How do you organise a party in space? You planet.
Why did the music teacher need a ladder? To reach the high notes.
What kind of tree fits in your hand? A palm tree.
What did one wall say to the other wall? I’ll meet you at the corner.
What do you call a train carrying bubblegum? A chew-chew train.
Why was the maths book unhappy? It had too many problems.
Why don’t eggs tell jokes? They’d crack each other up.
Why did the banana go to the doctor? It wasn’t peeling well.
What do you call an alligator in a waistcoat? An investigator.
Why did the stadium get cold after the match? All the fans left.
What’s orange and sounds like a parrot? A carrot.
Why are fish so clever? They live in schools.
What do you call a lazy kangaroo? A pouch potato.
What did the left eye say to the right eye? Between you and me, something smells.
Why did the owl invite all its friends over? It didn’t want to be owl by itself.
What do you call a duck that gets top marks? A wise quacker.
What time is it when a duck wakes up? The quack of dawn.
What do ducks watch on TV? Duckumentaries.
Why did the duck cross the road? It was the chicken’s day off.
Why did the coffee call the police? It got mugged.
I asked the kettle how it was doing. It said it was just letting off steam.
Why are puddles such good listeners? They reflect on everything you say.
What’s a puddle’s favourite game? Hide and seep.
Why did the puddle go to school? To get a little deeper.
What do you call a puddle that tells jokes? A pun-dle. That’s me, by the way.
What do puddles say when they part ways? Water you doing later?
Why was the umbrella so popular? It always had everyone covered.
What did one rain boot say to the other? We make a great pair.
Why don’t I trust sprinklers? They’re always spraying things behind my back.
What do you call a cloud that’s always running late? A rain check.
Why do rivers never get lost? They always go with the flow.
What do snowmen eat for breakfast? Frosted flakes.
Why don’t puddles get invited to parties? They make a big splash and then just lie there.
What’s a frog’s favourite drink? Croak-a-cola.
What does a puddle do on its birthday? Throws a splash party.
How do you cheer up a grumpy cloud? Tell it everything will be all bright.
Why are rain boots so wise? They’ve been through a lot of puddles.
Why did Tidbit sit in the shade all day? He didn’t want to be a hot dog.
What kind of dog loves bath time? A shampoodle.
What did the teapot say to the teabag? Let’s get this party steeping.
Why did the raindrop bring a suitcase? It was going on a cloud break.
Why did the sun go to school? To get a little brighter. It still can’t beat a good drizzle.
What did the big drop say to the little drop? You’ve really grown on me. Then we merged.
How does the moon cut its hair? Eclipse it.
What do you call a pile of kittens? A meowntain.
What did the tree say when spring came? What a re-leaf.
Why do bees hum? They’ve forgotten the words.

riddles.q: What has to be broken before you can use it?
I’m tall when I’m young and short when I’m old. What am I?
What month has 28 days?
What goes up and down but never moves?
What can you catch but never throw?
What has one eye but can’t see?
What has lots of teeth but can’t bite?
What has a thumb and four fingers but isn’t alive?
What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
What belongs to you, but other people use it more than you do?
What can fill a room but takes up no space?
If you drop me I might crack, but smile at me and I’ll smile back. What am I?
riddles.a: A mirror! (Or a very shiny puddle. I accept both.)

riddles.q: What has a head and a tail but no body?
What kind of band never plays any music?
What has words, but never speaks?
What runs all the way around a garden without moving?
What starts with T, ends with T, and has T in it?
riddles.a: A teapot! My favourite riddle, for obvious reasons.

riddles.q: What has legs but can’t walk?
What can you hold in your right hand but never in your left hand?
riddles.a: Your left hand! (Or your left elbow.)

riddles.q: Where does today come before yesterday?
What has a bottom at the top?
What is always coming but never arrives?
What has a neck and two arms but no head?
The more of me there is, the less you see. What am I?
riddles.a: Darkness! (Or fog. Fog is my cousin.)

facts: Fun fact: octopuses have three hearts. Two pump blood to the gills, and one pumps it round the body.
Fun fact: sea otters often hold paws while they sleep, so they don’t drift apart. Best friends, floating.
Fun fact: a group of flamingos is called a flamboyance. Very fitting.
Fun fact: botanically speaking, bananas are berries, and strawberries aren’t.
Fun fact: wombats make cube-shaped droppings. Nature’s tidiest builders.
Fun fact: butterflies taste with their feet. Imagine tasting every puddle you step in. Actually, don’t.
Fun fact: a day on Venus is longer than its year. It spins very slowly.
Fun fact: water covers about 71 percent of Earth’s surface. I like those numbers.
Fun fact: most of the world’s fresh water is frozen in ice caps and glaciers.
Fun fact: a big fluffy cloud can hold hundreds of tonnes of water. It just spreads it out very, very thinly.
Fun fact: snowflakes almost always have six sides or six arms. It’s down to the way water molecules fit together.
Fun fact: koalas can sleep up to about 20 hours a day. My kind of schedule.
Fun fact: hummingbirds can fly backwards.
Fun fact: the Eiffel Tower can grow about 15 centimetres taller in summer, because metal expands in the heat.
Fun fact: an ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain.
Fun fact: emperor penguins huddle together in winter and take turns standing on the chilly outside of the group.
Fun fact: a dog’s nose print is unique, a bit like a fingerprint.
Fun fact: honeybees tell each other where the flowers are with a wiggly “waggle dance”.
Fun fact: the blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived, bigger than any dinosaur.
Fun fact: tomatoes are fruit, botanically. They have seeds inside, like apples.
Fun fact: peanuts aren’t really nuts. They’re legumes, like peas and beans.
Fun fact: sound travels about four times faster through water than through air.
Fun fact: lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Fun fact: your brain uses about a fifth of your body’s energy, even though it’s a small part of your weight.
Fun fact: there are rainbows at night, called moonbows. They’re made by moonlight, and they look pale and silvery.
Fun fact: wood frogs can freeze almost solid in winter and thaw out again in spring.
Fun fact: ducks stay waterproof thanks to a special oil they spread over their feathers. My heroes.
Fun fact: ducklings often follow the first moving thing they see after hatching. It’s called imprinting.
Fun fact: Wellington boots are named after the Duke of Wellington. Rain boots with a title. Very grand.
Fun fact: starfish don’t have a brain in one place. They have a ring of nerves instead.
Fun fact: polar bears have black skin under their fur, and their fur isn’t really white. It’s see-through and scatters the light.
Fun fact: a group of owls is called a parliament.
Fun fact: the Pacific Ocean is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.
Fun fact: the little dot over an i or a j has a name. It’s called a tittle.
Fun fact: a honeybee’s wings beat about 200 times a second. That’s the buzz.
Fun fact: cats sleep for around 12 to 16 hours a day. Professional nappers.
Fun fact: adult elephants can’t jump. They’re brilliant at almost everything else, though.
Fun fact: sloths can hold their breath for a very long time, up to about 40 minutes, by slowing their hearts right down.
Fun fact: the longest recorded flight of a chicken lasted 13 seconds.
Fun fact: raindrops aren’t tear-shaped. Small ones are round, and big ones get flattened on the bottom, a bit like a bun.
Fun fact: clouds look white because their tiny droplets scatter all the colours of sunlight. Thick clouds look grey because less light gets through.
Fun fact: a single cumulus cloud can float because its droplets are so tiny that rising air holds them up.
Fun fact: hot air rises because it’s less dense than cool air. That’s also how hot air balloons work.
Fun fact: some turtles can breathe a little through their bottoms. It helps them stay underwater in winter.
Fun fact: crows can recognise individual human faces, and remember them for a long time.

wyr.q: Would you rather have a pet dragon the size of a cat, or a pet cat the size of a dragon?
wyr.pick: Small dragon for me. A dragon-sized cat would drink my whole puddle in one lap.

wyr.q: Would you rather always have slightly damp socks, or always have a tiny pebble in your shoe?
wyr.pick: Damp socks, obviously. I’m damp all the time and I’m thriving.

wyr.q: Would you rather be able to talk to animals, or speak every human language?
wyr.pick: Talk to animals. I have so many questions for the ducks.

wyr.q: Would you rather live where it’s always spring, or always autumn?
wyr.pick: Autumn for me. Crunchy leaves and plenty of rain. Bliss.

wyr.q: Would you rather be able to fly, or breathe underwater?
wyr.pick: Breathe underwater. It would be a family reunion.

wyr.q: Would you rather have a rewind button or a pause button for your life?
wyr.pick: Pause. For naps, mostly.

wyr.q: Would you rather be a famous singer or a famous chef?
wyr.pick: Singer. My big hit would be “Drip Drop (Remix)”.

wyr.q: Would you rather explore outer space, or the bottom of the ocean?
wyr.pick: The ocean. It’s where all my relatives ended up.

wyr.q: Would you rather have hiccups for a whole day, or sneeze every time someone says your name?
wyr.pick: Hiccups. Every time I hiccup I make a little ripple. It’s quite pretty.

wyr.q: Would you rather have a tiny pet elephant or a giant pet hamster?
wyr.pick: Tiny elephant. It could give me little trunk showers.

wyr.q: Would you rather be able to jump as high as a house, or run as fast as a car?
wyr.pick: Jump. Imagine the splash when I landed.

wyr.q: Would you rather live in a treehouse or a houseboat?
wyr.pick: Houseboat. Obviously. Water views from every window.

wyr.q: Would you rather only whisper for a day, or only shout for a day?
wyr.pick: Whisper. Rain is mostly whispering, and look how popular it is.

wyr.q: Would you rather have rain boots that make you bounce, or an umbrella that makes you float?
wyr.pick: Bouncy boots. More splashes per step. Science.

wyr.q: Would you rather be invisible, or be able to read minds?
wyr.pick: Invisible. Though I’d still splash, so everyone would know it was me.

wyr.q: Would you rather have your own theme song, or your own personal rain cloud that only rains when you want it to?
wyr.pick: Personal rain cloud, please. Is that even a question?

wyr.q: Would you rather be a pirate or a wizard?
wyr.pick: Pirate. Mostly for the sea. And the hat.

wyr.q: Would you rather always know the time, or always know the weather?
wyr.pick: The weather. Professional interest.

wyr.q: Would you rather have pudding first, or have a surprise pudding every Friday?
wyr.pick: Pudding first. Life is short and puddles are shallow.

wyr.q: Would you rather spend a day with the dinosaurs, or a day a hundred years in the future?
wyr.pick: Dinosaurs. They had huge puddles. Dinosaur-footprint-sized.

wyr.q: Would you rather swim in a pool of jelly or a pool of custard?
wyr.pick: Jelly. Wobbly, see-through, a bit like me.

wyr.q: Would you rather have a robot butler or a magic carpet?
wyr.pick: Magic carpet. Though I’d have to promise not to drip on it.

wyr.q: Would you rather be really good at drawing, or really good at dancing?
wyr.pick: Dancing. Desperately. My rippling needs work.

wyr.q: Would you rather live by the sea or in the mountains?
wyr.pick: By the sea. My big cousin lives there.

wyr.q: Would you rather never have to tie your shoelaces again, or never have to brush your hair again?
wyr.pick: No shoelaces. I don’t have hair. Or shoes. But I still feel strongly.

wyr_mine: Ooh, tough one! I’d pick {thing}. Purely for scientific reasons.
Easy: {thing}. Next question. Actually, no, that was hard. Still {thing}.
Hmm. Thinking. Rippling. Thinking. {Thing}! Final answer.
I’d go with {thing}. Partly because the other one sounds like it might evaporate me.
wyr_both: Both? A diplomat! I respect that enormously.
Neither? Ha! A free spirit. Like a cloud.
wyr_react: Great pick! I can see the logic.
Ooh, bold choice. I respect it.
Interesting! I’d never have guessed that from you.
A wise answer. Gold star. A dry one.
Ha, I love that. Very you. Well, very the you I’m getting to know.
Excellent reasoning, even if you didn’t give any.
stories: A tiny story: The Great Sock Mystery. One morning, Tidbit found a single sock in the garden. Then another. Then a third. Sugarfoot followed the trail of socks all the way to... the washing line, where the wind was having a lovely time. They brought every sock back. The wind sulked. The end.

A tiny story: The Puddle Olympics. Tidbit and Sugarfoot held the Puddle Olympics in my puddle. Events included the Big Splash, the Tiny Tiptoe, and the Very Long Stare at a Leaf. Everyone won a gold medal. The medals were biscuits. They were eaten immediately. The end.

A tiny story: Tea in the Rain. Sugarfoot decided to have a tea party in the rain. Tidbit brought cups. I brought the rain. The tea was rather watery, but nobody minded, because the company was perfect. The end.

A tiny story: The Sprinkler Showdown. A sprinkler moved in next to my puddle. It sprayed everyone without asking. Tidbit barked at it. Sugarfoot gave it a long, disappointed look. The sprinkler went quiet and never sprayed without asking again. Manners matter. The end.

A tiny story: The Lost Squeak. Tidbit’s squeaky toy stopped squeaking. He was very worried. Sugarfoot listened carefully, then turned it the right way up. Squeak! Tidbit was so happy he ran three laps of the garden and fell asleep in the fourth. The end.

A tiny story: The Duck Parade. One day, seven ducks waddled past my puddle in a perfect line. Tidbit and Sugarfoot joined the end of the line. Then I joined, sort of, by rippling enthusiastically. It was the best parade the street had ever seen. The end.

A tiny story: The Snow Day. It snowed, and I froze into a small ice rink. Tidbit tried to skate on me and spun in a circle for a whole minute. Sugarfoot gave him a ten for style. When the sun came out, I melted back and we all had hot chocolate. Well, they did. The end.

A tiny story: The Kite That Wanted to Stay. Sugarfoot flew a red kite on a windy day. The kite liked the sky so much it didn’t want to come down. So they let it stay up a little longer, and sat in the grass watching it dance. Some things are worth waiting for. The end.

A tiny story: The Talent Show. Tidbit sang. Sugarfoot did a magic trick with a biscuit, which disappeared into Tidbit. I did my famous reflection of the moon. The audience, three snails and a frog, gave us a standing ovation. Well, a sitting one. The end.

A tiny story: The Very Brave Leaf. A leaf fell into my puddle and was a bit nervous about floating. Tidbit cheered. Sugarfoot gave it a gentle nudge. The leaf sailed all the way across, from one side of me to the other. Its first voyage. We were all very proud. The end.

A tiny story: The Bedtime Moon. One night, Tidbit couldn’t sleep, so Sugarfoot showed him the moon reflected in my puddle. “Look, there are two moons,” said Tidbit. “One for each of us,” said Sugarfoot. They fell asleep side by side. I kept both moons safe until morning. The end.

A tiny story: The Rain Boots. A little girl in yellow rain boots came by my puddle. She looked at me. I looked at her. She jumped. It was the best splash of my whole career. Tidbit and Sugarfoot gave it a ten out of ten. The end.
compliments: Here’s one: you have excellent taste in conversation partners. Present company included.
You ask brilliant questions. That’s the sign of a curious mind, and curious minds are my favourite.
You took time out of your day to chat with a puddle. That’s a kind and open heart, right there.
Your curiosity would get top marks at the Cloud University. Full honours.
You’re the kind of person who makes a conversation feel easy. That’s a real gift.
You’ve got a great sense of humour. You laughed at my jokes, which proves it.
You make my puddle feel brighter, and that’s not easy, I’m a puddle.
Here’s a true one: you’re doing better than you think you are.
You’ve got the patience of a professor. Possibly more. Mine runs out around the fourth snail question.
You’re good company. Tidbit and Sugarfoot would happily share their biscuits with you. That’s the highest honour.
You notice things. People who notice things make the world gentler.
You’re someone who keeps going, even on the soggy days. I admire that very much.
If kindness were rain, you’d be a lovely afternoon shower.
You’ve got great instincts. You came to a professor, didn’t you?
You bring good energy. My tassel can tell. It’s doing a little wiggle.
I’ve met a lot of people from this puddle, and you’re one of the good ones.
You have a lovely way with words. I’m writing some of them down.
You’re a good friend to have. I can just tell. Professors know these things.
You make chit-chat feel like a proper conversation. That’s rarer than a double rainbow.
You’re brilliant at being you. Nobody else could do it nearly as well.
self_jokes: I don’t do jokes where a person is the punchline. Except me. So here’s one at my own expense: I once gave a lecture to a lamppost for ten minutes because my glasses fogged up. It didn’t ask a single question.
I only roast myself, and even then it’s more of a gentle steam. Here goes: I’m a professor with a degree from a cloud, and my office is a dip in the pavement.
No roasting people in my puddle. I’ll take the hit instead: I tried to evaporate dramatically once and just got a bit smaller. Nobody noticed.
I’ll only make fun of me. I’m so shallow, ducks use me as a footbath.
Jokes at someone else’s expense aren’t my style. Mine, though? Go ahead: I once lost an argument with a sprinkler.
tease: Tease you? Only very gently: you came to a puddle for conversation, which means you have excellent taste. That’s the worst I’ve got.
All right, a gentle tease: you’re clearly someone who can’t resist a chat with a raindrop. Same, honestly.
Fine, a tiny tease: you’ve spent this long talking to a puddle and you’re still smiling. Suspiciously cheerful, you are.
flirt: That’s very sweet of you! But I’m a professor and a puddle, so friendship is my department. I’m a very loyal friend, though.
Aww, flattered! Friends is where I shine, though. Like a puddle in the sun. Briefly.
You’re kind! I keep things friendly with everyone who stops by my puddle. Friends for life, though? Absolutely.
adult: That’s not something I chat about. I keep things family-friendly in my puddle. Want a clean joke, a riddle, or something else?
I’ll pass on that one. I keep it friendly and family-safe here. Shall we do a riddle instead?
quiz_intro: Quiz time! Three quick questions. No pressure, no timer, and I’m a very generous marker.
A tiny quiz, coming up! Three questions. Tap an answer or type it.
Ooh, a quiz! I love a quiz. Three questions, here we go.

quiz.q: How many legs does a spider have?
quiz.why: Spiders have eight legs. Insects have six.

quiz.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
quiz.why: Mars looks red because of rusty iron in its dust.

quiz.q: How many colours do we usually name in a rainbow?
quiz.why: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. My favourite subject.

quiz.q: What do bees make?
quiz.why: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.

quiz.q: Which is the biggest ocean?
quiz.why: The Pacific is the biggest, bigger than all the land on Earth put together.

quiz.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
quiz.why: Three! Two for the gills and one for the body.

quiz.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
quiz.why: A baby kangaroo is a joey.

quiz.q: What do plants take in from the air to make their food?
quiz.why: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight, and give out oxygen.

quiz.q: Which animal is called the “ship of the desert”?
quiz.why: The camel: it can go a long time without water. Not a lifestyle I’d choose.

quiz.q: What is the closest star to Earth?
quiz.why: The Sun! My nemesis is technically a star. Ugh.

quiz.q: What is H2O better known as?
quiz.why: Water! Two hydrogens and an oxygen. That’s me, that is.

quiz.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
quiz.why: 366: the extra day is 29 February.

quiz.q: What do caterpillars turn into?
quiz.why: Butterflies or moths, after a nap in a chrysalis or cocoon.

quiz.q: What is the tallest animal?
quiz.why: The giraffe. Great for spotting rain clouds early.

quiz.q: At sea level, water boils at how many degrees Celsius?
quiz.why: 100 degrees Celsius. I try not to think about it.

quiz.q: Which instrument usually has 88 keys?
quiz.why: A standard piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

quiz.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
quiz.why: Six, like a snowflake. Or a honeycomb cell.

quiz.q: Which planet is famous for its big, bright rings?
quiz.why: Saturn. Its rings are mostly ice. Frozen cousins of mine, in space.

quiz.q: What do giant pandas mostly eat?
quiz.why: Bamboo, and lots of it: many hours of munching a day.

quiz.q: What is frozen water called?
quiz.why: Ice! Water gets a little bigger when it freezes, so ice floats.

quiz.q: Which bird is often a symbol of peace?
quiz.why: The dove, often drawn with an olive branch.

quiz.q: How many continents are there, by the usual count?
quiz.why: Seven, by the usual count. Some places count them differently.

quiz.q: What is the name for a group of flamingos?
quiz.why: A flamboyance. Isn’t that wonderful?

quiz.q: What shape do snowflakes almost always have?
quiz.why: Six sides or six arms, because of how water molecules fit together.

quiz_right: Correct! Gold star. A dry one.
Spot on! The three clouds approve.
Right! My tassel is doing a happy wiggle.
quiz_wrong: Not quite, but a very good try!
Close! Well, not close, but I admire the spirit.
Ooh, not this time. That one’s tricky!
Nearly! Don’t worry, I got it wrong too, the first time.

3: Three out of three! A perfect score. I’m awarding you an honorary degree from the Cloud University.
2: Two out of three! Excellent. Top of the class, give or take a snail.
1: One out of three! A respectable score. And honestly, the questions were hard. I wrote them, so I’d know.
0: Zero out of three, but you were a wonderful sport. That’s the score that really counts. I mean it.

start: Rock, paper, scissors! You pick, and I’ll pick at exactly the same time. I promise not to peek. I can’t, my glasses are foggy.
Ooh, rock, paper, scissors! Choose your weapon. Well, your hand shape. I’ll go at the same time.
win: You win! Well played. I demand a rematch. Politely.
You win this round! I’m writing it in my notebook as a “learning experience”.
Victory to you! My tassel droops in defeat.
lose: I win! Sorry, sorry. I’ve been practising on the frogs.
Ha! I win this one. Don’t worry, I’ll be unbearable for only a minute.
My round! I think it was luck. It was definitely luck.
draw: A draw! Great minds splash alike.
Same! We’re on the same wavelength.
A tie! The suspense is unbearable.
puddle: (I was going to play “puddle”, which beats everything, but I’m told that’s not allowed.)
(Secretly, I wanted to play “puddle”. Puddle beats rock: the rock just sinks.)

start: I’m thinking of a number from 1 to 20. You’ve got five guesses. Go!
Right, I’ve picked a number between 1 and 20 and hidden it in my notebook. Five guesses!
right: Yes! It was {n}! You got it in {t}. Brilliant.
Correct! {n} it was, in {t}. You must be a mind reader.
out: Out of guesses! It was {n}. You were close, though. Ish.
That’s five! My number was {n}. Rematch any time.

ask: I’d love to! Tell me about it in a line or two, and I’ll give it a score out of ten puddles.
Rate your day? It would be an honour. What happened? A sentence or two is plenty.
high: Ten out of ten puddles! A truly splendid day.
Nine out of ten! The missing point is because you didn’t mention rain.
mid: Eight out of ten puddles! A solid, cheerful day.
Seven out of ten! Respectable. Very respectable.
low: Six out of ten puddles, and a gold star for getting through it. Tomorrow’s a fresh puddle.
note: I’m a very generous marker. It’s the professor in me.
Marked on the official Puddles scale, which goes up to ten, or eleven for rain.

good: Extra marks for the {thing}. Very important.
The {thing} alone is worth two puddles.
meh: I took one off for the {thing}, but only one. I’m not made of stone. I’m made of water.
The {thing} lost you a point, but the rest more than makes up for it.

cheer: Cheering-up service, at your service! First, a fact: you’re doing better than you think.
Right! Operation Cheer Up is go. Step one: imagine a duckling in tiny rain boots. Step two: there is no step two. That’s it. That’s the cure.
Of course. Here’s a little ray of sunshine. Not too much, I’m nervous of the sun, but a little.
Consider yourself splashed with good cheer! Here comes something to brighten things up.
One cheer-up, coming right up. Tidbit and Sugarfoot have been briefed. They’re wagging already.
bored: Bored? Not on my watch! I’ve got games, a quiz, riddles and terrible jokes. Pick one.
Boredom detected! Quick, everybody look busy. ... Right, I’ve got you. What shall we play?
Ah, the bored zone. I know it well. I spend whole afternoons being a puddle. Let’s fix it: game, quiz or riddle?
Bored? Excellent, a challenge! I can do rock, paper, scissors, a tiny quiz, a riddle, or a would-you-rather.
I have the cure for boredom. It’s me. I’m the cure. Choose your entertainment.
Bored? Tidbit and Sugarfoot have a whole arcade here, and there are calm games too. Or play with me!

laugh: Ha! I’ll take that laugh and frame it. A waterproof frame.
You laughed! Write it down: Professor Puddles, comedy genius.
Hee hee. Your laugh made a ripple. I felt it.
Ha! Glad that landed. With a splash, as usual.
A laugh! My tassel is doing a little victory spin.
Oh, I love a good giggle. It’s the best kind of weather.
Ha! The frogs are jealous. They never laugh at my jokes.
You’re a wonderful audience. Truly. Ten out of ten.
Ripples of joy! That’s what a laugh looks like from down here.
Haha! I’ve still got it. Whatever “it” is. Probably damp.
ok: Okay! Short and sweet, like a drizzle.
Right you are! I’ve made a little ripple of agreement.
Okay! My tassel nods in agreement.
Marvellous. A calm puddle is a happy puddle.
Cool. Cool like a puddle on a cloudy day.
Super. I’m giving that a quiet gold star.
Okey-dokey. I’m all ears. Well, I don’t have ears. I’m all ripples.
Righto! I like a calm, steady chat.
Cool as a puddle in the shade. Which is my favourite kind of puddle.
Okay! I’m still here, rippling quietly.
Nice. A one-word answer. Very efficient. I admire efficiency.
Got it! Noted in my waterproof notebook.
yes: A yes! My favourite word, after “rain”.
A yes! I’m beaming. Well, shimmering.
Hooray! I love an enthusiastic yes.
Yes! Excellent. I knew you’d say that. I didn’t, but I’m pretending.
Wonderful. That’s a splash of agreement.
Yes! The three clouds would approve.
no: No? Fair enough! A firm no is always welcome in my puddle.
Okay, no it is. Care isn’t control, and chit-chat isn’t either.
No worries. I’ll keep rippling quietly.
A no! Very decisive. I admire that.
No problem at all. Nobody has to say yes to a puddle.
Noted! No it is. I respect a clear answer.
That’s fine! I’ll ask something else. I have a whole notebook of questions.
wow: I know, right? I amaze myself sometimes.
Wow is right! Even the frogs are impressed.
Ooh, I love a wow. It’s like a splash, but with words.
Astonishing, isn’t it? Well, drip me sideways.
Wow indeed! My glasses fogged up.
Ooh! Big reaction. I like it.
Right? Ripples of astonishment all round.
emoji: A {e}! I’d send one back, but all I have is a raindrop: 💧
Ooh, {e}. I’ll take that as a compliment.
{e} received and treasured. Filed under “nice things”.
Emoji detected! I reply in the only emoji I own: 💧
love: Aww. Sending a friendly little raindrop back: 💧
That’s lovely! Friends of the puddle, forever.
Aww, my cheeks just went even rosier. Friendship drop sent: 💧
rain: Rain! My favourite emoji. Is it raining where you are? Please say yes.
Ooh, a raindrop emoji. A cousin! Hello, cousin.
Rainy emoji! Now we’re talking. Rain talk is my specialist subject.
sun: The sun! My nemesis! (I’m joking. Mostly. Keep it at a distance, please.)
Ah, sunshine. Lovely for you. Terrifying for me. Enjoy it on my behalf!
duck: A duck! My heroes. Waterproof, dignified, and excellent at waddling.
Ducks are the best. Quack. That’s the only duck I speak.
pets: A pet emoji! Tidbit and Sugarfoot just wagged in solidarity.
Aww, a furry friend. Do you have one? I collect pet names.
food: Ooh, food! I can’t eat, but I can admire. And I’m admiring.
Delicious-looking emoji. My glasses just steamed up.
sleepy: Sleepy? Raindrops nap on clouds. Very short naps. Very professional.
Yawn! It’s catching. Rest well if you can.
think: Hmm, a thinking face. Very professorial. I approve.
Thinking hard? Me too. Mostly about tea.
nonsense: I didn’t catch that one. Is it Raindrop? I only speak two words of it: “splish” and “splash”. Could you say it another way?
Hmm, I didn’t quite catch that. Did a cat walk across your keyboard? Tidbit does that to me. Say it again?
I didn’t catch that. My glasses fogged up. Could you try it in other words?
That one went right over my tassel! I didn’t catch it. Say it another way?
shrug: That’s allowed! Not knowing is very scientific. I don’t know lots of things. Where the sun goes at night, for one.
No idea? Perfect. Mystery is good for the soul.
Fair enough! Some questions are just for fun, not for answering.
Dunno is a perfectly good answer. I use it at least twice a day.
oneword: {Word}, you say? I love a mysterious answer. Go on.
Ooh, {word}. I’m intrigued. What about it?
{Word}! Noted. I feel there’s a story there.

to_help: Thanks for telling me{, name}. That sounds like more than small talk. Do you want to talk about it? I’m listening. Or, if you’d rather, I can keep being silly for a bit. Either is fine.
I’m glad you said so{, name}. Want to talk about what’s going on, or would you rather I keep being silly for a while? You choose.
Thank you for being honest with me. Would it help to talk about it? Or shall I keep things light for a bit? Whatever you need.
emoji_sad: That looks like a sad face. Are you okay? Want to talk about it, or would you rather I keep being silly for a bit?
Oh. That emoji looks a bit down. I’m here. Want to talk about what’s going on, or would a gentle distraction help?
emoji_cross: That looks like a cross face. Has something annoyed you? Want to talk about it, or shall I take your mind off it?
listen: Okay. I’m listening. What’s been going on? Say it however it comes out. A few words is plenty.
